findings.title: Extension cannot be loaded as extensions=['external_links']: no entry point in pyproject.toml
findings.evidence: Maintainer decision 1 says the extension is loaded with `extensions=['external_links']`, and ARCHITECTURE.md constraint 4 says every built-in extension needs an entry point under [project.entry-points.'markdown.extensions']. The diff adds no entry point; the list ends at `legacy_em` (line 91). Running `python -c "import markdown; markdown.markdown('[d](https://e.com)', extensions=['external_links'])"` fails with: ModuleNotFoundError No module named 'external_links'. Fix: add `external_links = 'markdown.extensions.external_links:ExternalLinksExtension'` and reinstall.

findings.title: Tests skip the short-name loading and most of the cases the issue lists
findings.evidence: Both tests pass an `ExternalLinksExtension()` instance, so the missing entry point goes unnoticed. The maintainer explicitly listed automatic links (`<https://example.com>`), `http://`, `#anchors`, `mailto:` and images, and none of them has a test. Add tests that use `extensions=['external_links']` and cover each of these cases.

notes: The treeprocessor at priority 3 runs after the inline treeprocessor (20) and before prettify, so it sees autolinks and reference links. The behaviour is correct when the extension is passed as an instance.
Raw HTML `<a href="https://...">` is stashed and not changed. That seems acceptable because the issue only covers Markdown links, but it could be documented.
There is no docs page for the new extension under docs/extensions/ (no blocking).

own_checks.check: Extension loads by its short name 'external_links'
Automatic link <https://example.com> gets target and rel
http:// links and reference-style links are marked
own_checks.output_excerpt: <a href="http://e.com" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">; <a href="https://e.com" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">

own_checks.check: mailto: links, #anchors and images are unchanged

summary: The link rewriting works when the extension is passed as an instance: external http/https links, autolinks and reference links are marked, while mailto, anchors and images are left alone. But the PR adds no pyproject entry point, so `extensions=['external_links']` raises ModuleNotFoundError. That breaks maintainer decision 1 and ARCHITECTURE.md constraint 4. The tests miss this because they only use instances.
